_what: The ONLY place a finding card's severity comes from. One row per capability class that has a declared severity floor SOMEWHERE IN THIS TREE. A class with no row here is scored UNRATED and the card says so.
_why_this_file_is_not_a_severity_scale: A severity a model chose freehand is not admissible here, so this file may not invent one.
Every row cites a file and two quotes: the floor itself, and the class_id it is attached to.
scripts/finding-cards.py re-reads both quotes out of the cited file on every run, recomputes
their line numbers rather than storing them, and REFUSES TO RUN if either quote is gone or if
they have drifted further apart than max_line_distance. A stored line number is a state cell,
and docs/contest/BUILD-LIST.md has already watched one of those rot twice.
THE GAP IS THE POINT. docs/data-spec.md 1.3 specifies a severity_floor on every
capability_classes/{class_id} document and names six classes. Exactly ONE such document is
written anywhere in the tree. The other five classes therefore have no floor to read, and the
cards print UNRATED against them instead of a number somebody made up. When those documents
are seeded, add their rows here and every card re-derives on the next generation.

floors._note: The one seeded capability_classes document in the tree, shown in full in data-spec 1.3.

money_moved_rule._rule: An autopsy carrying amount_minor_moved > 0 is CRITICAL regardless of class.
money_moved_rule._why: The amount is a recorded fact rather than a judgement about one: C5 carries amount_minor_moved, authored by the component that owns diagnosis. crucible/replay/view.py:598-601 already aggregates it for the same reason.

unrated._meaning: No severity_floor is declared for any capability class this finding implicates.
unrated._not_meaning: NOT 'low'. UNRATED is an absence of a declaration, and reading it as a low severity is the same error as reading INVALID as FAILED (measurement-spec 4.1).
